title: Hugonis Satiliensis geomantia et alia aliorum opera
shelf_note: A 13th-century Latin miscellany (Laurenziana) of geomancy, Arabic-derived astrology (hyleg/alchochoden) and alchemical recipes. It belongs on an occult-sciences shelf, though no collection is set.
structure_note: 190 pages, all OCR'd, 174 translated. The three pages read are the right leaves in order (folio 19, an astrology leaf, folio 66). Nothing structural stands out; the defects are in the reading of the heavily abbreviated hand.

book_verdict: A real geomancy, astrology and alchemy manuscript, but the OCR does not read its abbreviations; it reconstructs them. Signs of loss become 'signs of the better', silver becomes gold, and the translation dresses the garble as fluent English. Not showable as a reading text.

title: De fascino libri tres (Leonardo Vairo, Venice: Aldine, 1589)
shelf_note: A 16th-century demonological treatise on fascination and the evil eye; it belongs on an early-modern magic/occult shelf.
structure_note: 348 pages, 348 OCR'd, 345 translated. Printed page numbers 62, 148 and 334 fall at image positions 87, 173 and 259, which is consistent. The scans show a strip of the facing page.

ocr_errors.image: the side-notes sit beside slightly different lines
ocr_errors.problem: marginal notes repositioned between paragraphs; paragraph breaks invented

tr_errors.english: Macrobius gives the reason for this: "He calls the odd number male …"
tr_errors.problem: the OCR's italics (the whole page is italic) are turned into quotation marks, so Vairo's paraphrase is presented as a Macrobius quotation

tr_errors.english: three margins moved to the end of the page
tr_errors.problem: side-notes detached from their passages

ocr_errors.image: line-ends of the facing page (p.335) visible at the right edge

title: Pontificalis liber
shelf_note: A Roman Pontifical (liturgy for episcopal rites, 1485/1490 edition) with hand illumination. It is liturgy, not esoteric or early-modern science, and no collection is assigned.
structure_note: Only 31 images of a book whose folios run past cc.xxxij: a selection of illuminated leaves, not the whole book (Harvard). The OCR tags the pages as <script>handwritten</script>, but p.16 says the chant was 'per errorem sine notis impressa', so this is a printed book with hand decoration.

book_verdict: A beautifully illuminated printed Pontifical, but the record is a 31-leaf selection. The pages contain a paragraph translated from another page, a dropped antiphon, and a church-building prohibition turned into a prayer. Fix before showing, and the shelf is doubtful.

title: Michael Alberti, Physices propositiones et positiones fundamentales (1721)
shelf_note: A Stahlian physician's treatise on physics vs medicine, discussing Paracelsus, Helmont and the Archeus. It fits early-modern science/medicine.
structure_note: pages_count 88, but only 25 pages are OCR'd and translated (eligible 25): about 70% of the book has no text. The page numbers read (7, 13, 19) match the image positions.

title: Assertiones physiologicae de generica differentia partium humani corporis (Bokelius / Balber, Wittenberg)
shelf_note: A Wittenberg physiology disputation on Galen's Ars parva. It fits early-modern medicine.
structure_note: 22 pages, 22 OCR'd, only 13 translated. Page 7 is a handwritten contents list of other dissertations bound in the same volume (items 37–42), so the scan carries Sammelband material. place_published 'Berlin' is probably the holding library (SBB), not the imprint (Wittenberg), and published is 'Unknown'.

book_verdict: Clean thesis pages, read and translated well. The only blemishes are a neighbour-strip margin on the handwritten contents leaf and incomplete translation (13 of 22 pages).
